summary: Fixed a misleading fleet-map glyph: every appliance pin (the floor-editor marker and placing cursor, the twin-tree rail leaf, the inspector's ApplianceCard, and the read-only floor drill-down) picked its icon by node kind - camera/cpu/door - so a mymatasan recorder drew the same camera icon as an actual camera pinned beside it, and a mypintusan door controller drew a door. The icon showed what the box watches or controls rather than what it is. Added a new shared glyph, `board`, to frontend/shared/src/icons.js (a single-board computer: board outline, its SoC, and a pin header - what a fleet appliance actually is, a mini PC or a Raspberry Pi in a box, as distinct from the existing bare-chip `cpu` glyph and the `video` camera glyph) and switched every myseliasan appliance marker to that one glyph regardless of kind; a camera placement still draws the camera icon. The per-kind KIND_ICON/PLACING_ICON lookup maps and their now-unused nodeKindOf imports were removed from floor_editor.js, map/inspector.js and map/twin_tree.js.
compatibility: Frontend-only icon change; no API, schema, or config changes. `icons.js` is shared by all five apps and the change is purely additive (one new key), verified by rebuilding mymatasan's frontend as well. Deliberate trade-off: the map no longer distinguishes an NVR from an IoT hub from a door controller by icon shape - kind is still legible from the row's own name, the tray's grouping, and the inspector's subtitle, and a truthful single icon was judged better than three misleading ones. No i18n change (all four dicts unchanged at an identical key count). Verified live on a throwaway install with a camera, an NVR, an IoT hub and a door controller pinned on the same plan: the camera draws the camera glyph and all three appliances draw the board glyph. Build, go test and npm run lint:undef clean, zero console errors.
